When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is verified (where the Type Approval Authority is not satisfied with the manufacturer's checking procedure), the broadband and narrowband electromagnetic disturbance levels measured shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits prescribed in paragraphs 6.5.2.1 and 6.6.2.1.

When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is verified (where the Type Approval Authority is not satisfied with the manufacturer's checking procedure), the ESA shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road user when subjected to a field strength, expressed in V/m, up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1.

When the conformity of a component or STU taken from the series is verified (where the Type Approval Authority is not satisfied with the manufacturer's checking procedure), the component or STU shall show no degradation of performance of immunity related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp) up to the conducted transient immunity levels given in paragraph 6.9.1.

When the conformity of a component or STU taken from the series is verified (where the Type Approval Authority is not satisfied with the manufacturer's checking procedure), the component or STU shall not exceed the conducted transient emission levels given in paragraph 6.7.1.

ESA broadband reference limits (paragraph 6.5.2.1), where broadband emission testing is not exempted under paragraph 6.10: the broadband electromagnetic radiation of the ESA (rear lamp LED electronics), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m from 30 to 75 MHz and E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m from 75 to 400 MHz (F in MHz).

ESA broadband reference limits (paragraph 6.5.2.1), where broadband emission testing is not exempted under paragraph 6.10: the broadband electromagnetic radiation of the ESA (rear lamp LED electronics), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed E = 63 dBµV/m from 400 to 1,000 MHz.

ESA narrowband reference limits (paragraph 6.6.2.1), where narrowband emission testing is not exempted under paragraph 6.10 (e.g. active electronic driver with oscillator/microcontroller): the narrowband electromagnetic radiation of the ESA (rear lamp LED electronics), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m from 30 to 75 MHz and E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m from 75 to 400 MHz (F in MHz).

ESA narrowband reference limits (paragraph 6.6.2.1), where narrowband emission testing is not exempted under paragraph 6.10 (e.g. active electronic driver with oscillator/microcontroller): the narrowband electromagnetic radiation of the ESA (rear lamp LED electronics), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed E = 53 dBµV/m from 400 to 1,000 MHz.
The measurement of broadband electromagnetic emissions from the ESA (rear lamp LED modules and driving circuitry) shall be performed according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 7.
During the broadband emission test the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
For an ESA not involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
The broadband emission limits for the ESA apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

Broadband emission measurements of the ESA may be performed with either quasi-peak or peak detectors; the limits of paragraph 6.5 are for quasi-peak detectors, and if peak detectors are used a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.
The measurement of narrowband electromagnetic emissions from the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 8.
During the narrowband emission test the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
The narrowband emission test of the ESA shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4 of CISPR 25.
The narrowband emission limits for the ESA apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
Narrowband emission measurements of the ESA shall be performed with an average detector.

For immunity to electromagnetic radiation, the ESA may comply with the requirements of any combination of the following test methods at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that the full frequency range of Annex 9 paragraph 3.1 is covered: absorber chamber test (ISO 11452-2), TEM cell testing (ISO 11452-3), bulk current injection testing (ISO 11452-4), stripline testing (ISO 11452-5), reverberation chamber test (ISO 11452-11); frequency range and general test conditions shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
The test conditions for the ESA radiated immunity test shall be according to ISO 11452-1.

During the radiated immunity test the ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition, arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
ESA radiated immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency step size and dwell time according to ISO 11452-1.

In the ESA radiated immunity test, the test signal modulation in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range shall be AM with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

In the ESA radiated immunity test, the test signal modulation in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

In the ESA radiated immunity test, the test signal modulation in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
Where the absorber chamber test is used, the 'substitution method' shall be used to establish the test field conditions according to ISO 11452-2.
Where the absorber chamber test is used, the test shall be performed with vertical polarization.
Where TEM cell testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3, with the method of maximum field coupling to the ESA or to the wiring harness inside the TEM cell.

Where bulk current injection testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench with either the substitution method and injection probe at 150 mm from the ESA, or the closed loop method and injection probe at 900 mm from the ESA; as an alternative the ESA may be tested installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4 with the substitution method and injection probe at 150 mm from the ESA.
Where stripline testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5.
Where the reverberation chamber test is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11, using a test setup with ground plane unless otherwise specified.
The ESA shall be immune to test pulse 1 according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
The ESA shall be immune to test pulse 2a according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
The ESA shall be immune to test pulse 2b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
The ESA shall be immune to test pulse 3a according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
The ESA shall be immune to test pulse 3b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The ESA shall be tested with the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other connections operationally connected to supply lines; ESAs exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (without 12 V/24 V starter motor) are not subject to the starting profile.

Emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 on supply lines and on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The external projection provisions of UN R26 do not apply to those parts of the lamp's external surface (outer lens, exposed housing rim or seal) which, with the vehicle in the laden condition and all doors, windows and access lids closed, are either at a height of more than 2 m, or below the floor line, or so located that, in their static condition as well as in operation, they cannot be contacted by a sphere 100 mm in diameter.

The lamp's external surface (outer lens, exposed housing rim/bezel or seal), as installed on the M1 vehicle, shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by the external surface or brushing against it in the event of a collision.
The lamp's external surface, as installed on the M1 vehicle, shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.

No protruding part of the lamp's external surface (outer lens edges, exposed housing rim/bezel edges) shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm; this does not apply to parts which protrude less than 5 mm, but the outward facing angles of such parts shall be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.

If a protruding part of the lamp's external surface (e.g. an exposed seal/gasket of TPE or silicone, or an edge with radius < 2.5 mm) is made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A, it may have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm; the hardness shall be measured with the component as installed on the vehicle, and where a Shore A measurement is impossible, comparable measurements shall be used for evaluation.
Production lamps fitted to the approved vehicle type shall be so manufactured that the vehicle conforms to the type approved by meeting the requirements of paragraphs 5. and 6. of UN R26.

Where the lamp protrudes beyond the nominal line of the panel and is mounted on a surface other than convex, if the dimension of the lamp's projection cannot be determined by simple measurement, the projection dimension shall be determined as the maximum variation of the distance of the centre of a 100 mm diameter sphere from the nominal line of the panel when the sphere is moved over the lamp while in constant contact with it (see Annex 3, Figure 3).
